theme: Praise the LORD from the heavens
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 148. This psalm calls every part of creation to praise: heavens, deeps, weather, mountains, animals, kings, and children. Read it aloud as a roll call.
settingTheScene: Psalm 148 is a hymn that commands praise from everything God has made. It is structured in two halves: praise from the heavens (vv. 1-6) and praise from the earth (vv. 7-14). You will read this psalm again in Unit 24. Today, read it as the response of the rebuilt city, standing on a wall whose stones, towers, and gates lie under the open sky.
observation: “Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights!” (v. 1).
“Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts!” (v. 2).
“Praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all you shining stars!” (v. 3).
“Let them praise the name of the LORD! For he commanded and they were created” (v. 5).
“Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all deeps” (v. 7).
“Fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling his word!” (v. 8).
“Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth! Young men and maidens together, old men and children!” (vv. 11-12).
“He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his saints” (v. 14).
interpretation:
The psalm is a vast choir. First the heavens: angels, hosts, sun, moon, stars, even “you waters above the heavens.” They praise because “he commanded and they were created.” Creation did not come from chance or from rival gods but from a spoken word. Everything in the sky exists by the will of God and is meant to bring him glory.

Then the earth: sea creatures, fire, hail, snow, stormy winds, mountains, fruit trees, cattle, creeping things, and flying birds. Notice the wildness. The deeps and the storms are not enemies of praise; even “stormy wind fulfilling his word.” The elements that frightened ancient people are in the choir. Creation praises by being what God made it to be.

Finally comes humanity: kings and peoples, young and old, men and women. Everyone, from the throne to the cradle, is summoned. Humans praise with words and wills, which the rest of creation cannot do. We give voice to the whole choir.

The reason for praise is that “his name alone is exalted; his majesty is above earth and heaven.” And then a surprising turn: “He has raised up a horn for his people.” The God of galaxies takes special notice of a small people. A horn meant strength and a ruler. For a community just rebuilt, it carried the hope of a coming king.

For you, the point is that praise is not a private act that fits in the margins. It is the purpose of everything that exists. When you praise, you join a choir that is as old as creation.
connection: Colossians 1:16 says all things were created through him and for him. Romans 8:19-22 says creation waits and groans for the revealing of the sons of God. Luke 1:69 says God “has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.” Philippians 2:10 says every knee will bow. Revelation 5:13 hears every creature in heaven and earth and under the earth and in the sea saying, “To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing.”
application:
Spend ten minutes outdoors. Name five things you see and thank God for each.

Praise God with your whole voice today, by singing or speaking aloud.

Notice how everything around you was commanded into being by God’s word.
prayerPrompts: Join creation in praising God, naming what in creation moves you.
Thank him that he commanded and you were created.
Praise him for raising up a horn for his people.
